name: Sonata Software Ltd
title: Sonata Software Ltd - 532221 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Sonata's international utilisation fell to 88.5% from 91.8% and EBITDA to 15.4% from 20.2%, with management giving no quantified margin or growth guidance and no capacity signal, leaving the Q2 recovery unproven.

summary.headline: Sonata Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10.6% YoY to Rs 3,279.1 Cr, but PAT fell 17.1% QoQ to Rs 108.6 Cr on Rs 35.4 Cr forex hit.
summary.overview: International services revenue was flat QoQ in constant currency (+0.1%) at $82 million, while EBITDA margin fell to 15.4% from 20.2% as utilisation dropped to 88.5% on a delayed large-deal ramp-up, a one-time compensation benefit reversed, and AI talent investments rose. Domestic revenue was Rs 2,505.6 Cr with gross contribution up 4.2% QoQ and 14.5% YoY, and management said an OEM direct-billing risk has been partly reversed through contract renewals. Management reiterated an AI-native, engineering-led strategy and an AI order book of $21.4 million, but declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin or formal guidance.

segments.name: International services
segments.commentary: Revenue $82M, flat QoQ cc and +2.1% YoY cc; EBITDA 15.4% vs 20.2% in Q4 on utilisation drop, one-time Q4 compensation benefit (~2 pts), ~50 bps forex hit and AI talent investments. Headcount 6,293 (vs 6,283), attrition 13%, offshore mix 70%.

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs 2,505.6 Cr and gross contribution Rs 78.5 Cr (+14.5% YoY). SMC and corporate software business grew ~82% YoY. DSO rose to 65 days from 47 days, which management attributed to seasonality.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA to show positive traction each quarter this year, with some one-time items normalising in coming quarters; it declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin as guidance.
Large-deal ramp-up expected to complete in Q2 FY27; management said margin trajectory should turn positive from next quarter.
Domestic management expects financial performance to keep improving in Q2 and the rest of the year.
Normalised effective tax rate guided at about 25%; Q1 benefited from a one-time US state R&D tax credit.
Medium-term: management expects gradual improvement in revenue and EBITDA, supported by AI pipeline.
capex_capacity: Utilisation at 88.5% vs 91.8% in Q4; attributed to delayed large-deal ramp-up and AI capability incubation.
Forward deployed engineer pool being expanded to about 100 people by August 2026.
Sonata University has trained 93% of workforce in AI.
Workbench agentic AI service delivery platform launched in the quarter; several clients have shown interest.
demand_pricing: AI order book $21.4M (18.2% of total order book) vs $16.9M in Q4; AI-led pipeline $340M; AI-led order wins +27% QoQ and AI-led pipeline +21% QoQ.

About seven new international customer wins in the quarter, including a three-year multimillion-dollar modernisation and managed services deal; a global beverage brand deal (800+ locations, 11 countries) was also won.
Top 10 clients were 51% of international revenue; management declined to disclose absolute top-10 revenue, which an analyst said declined QoQ.
Clients above $5M run rate: 12 (flat QoQ); $3-5M: 9 (flat QoQ); clients above $10M run rate: eight.
Management said 21% of engagements are output-based; cloud share of revenue reported at 62% vs 53% a year ago (per analyst question).
Domestic: some customers in the probable direct-billing list were retained through contract renewals after an OEM moved to direct billing with large customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the domestic business confident of sustaining double-digit YoY gross contribution growth, and how are the nine micro-verticals and six value pools defined?
qa_highlights.answer: Management (Jagannathan) said it is confident domestic growth momentum will continue as past issues are behind it. Rajsekhar said the six value pools are customer engagement and ops transformation, agentic AI, legacy modernisation, AI-ready data, resilient AI backbone and AI-native service delivery; micro-verticals include payments, mortgage and lending, healthcare, clinical ops, logistics and retail manufacturing, and are sharpened existing areas rather than new ones.

qa_highlights.question: Top-10 client revenue fell about 6% QoQ and has been weak for six quarters; is productivity pass-through the cause, and what is the absolute top-10 figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan attributed the lower top-10 share (51%) to growth in the 11-20 client bucket and new wins, with no discounts or productivity pass-through and no major top-10 account declining. He declined to disclose absolute top-10 revenue, citing risk of exposing top-5 client revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did BFSI/retail and manufacturing vertical revenue decline QoQ, and when will they recover; what is the outlook for TMT?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan said the BFSI share grew beyond expectations, so R&D as a percentage of revenue fell; this is not a standalone R&D issue. Rajsekhar said TMT growth will come from hyperscalers and enterprise product and packaged software organisations, with early pipeline signs from new leadership.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the international margin drop and how will the outcome/output-based model keep margins on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajsekhar said the large-deal ramp-up is largely behind, billing/paperwork delays were one-time, and AI advisory and forward-deployed engineer investments will continue for a couple more quarters; he expects a positive margin trajectory from next quarter. Jagannathan said the top-five accounts appear stable with no major threat, with growth expected in a few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net cash fall QoQ, and what is the cash conversion picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan said the decline reflects domestic vendor payouts tied to turnover and deal completions, with gross cash about Rs 565-567 Cr vs Rs 605 Cr and net cash about Rs 65 Cr vs Rs 30 Cr. He said there was no one-time payment and international collections and DSO were stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state international EBITDA margin, and what is the domestic large-deal margin view?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin, saying it would become guidance; he said margin will move positively in coming quarters. For the domestic large deal, management measures success by absolute gross contribution, which is positive and accretive, not by percentage margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised tax rate and does the R&D tax credit affect cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan said the normalised ETR is about 25%; Q1 benefited from a one-time US state R&D tax credit that reduces the cash tax liability.

risks_watch: Utilisation at 88.5% vs 91.8% in Q4; delayed large-deal ramp-up is said to complete in Q2 FY27 and any slippage would keep margins depressed.

International EBITDA margin at 15.4% vs 20.2% in Q4; management gives no steady-state margin, so the recovery path rests on one-time items normalising and investments paying off in a couple of quarters.
Top-10 client revenue fell about 6% QoQ per an analyst, with absolute figures undisclosed; the 11-20 client bucket and top-5 stability need to be tracked.
Domestic DSO rose to 65 days from 47 days (management calls it seasonal) and net cash fell to about Rs 65 Cr gross-to-net basis tied to vendor payouts.
Forex swings: about Rs 35.4 Cr PAT impact in Q1 and about 50 bps EBITDA hit; the Q1 PAT decline is driven by forex, and the tax benefit is one-time.

Management reiterated that the AI pipeline (Rs/USD 340M) and AI order book ($21.4M) must convert into revenue; the client count above $1M has fallen for several quarters, which management attributes to migration to higher buckets.
key_quotes: Base utilization continues to operate at 88.5% as we encountered a delay in a large deal ramp-up and AI capability incubation, which caused a slight reduction in the utilization.
I am not able to define a stable state EBITDA margin I do not want that will become a guidance kind of a nature, but definitely it will move towards a positive direction for us in the coming quarters
Overall, we should have a positive trajectory on our margin from next quarter onwards as we go forward.
We are confident that the financial performance will further continue to improve in Q2 and during rest of the financial year.
summary.management_tone: Management is confident on strategy and AI pipeline momentum, but cautious on near-term numbers: it declined to give a steady-state EBITDA margin or guidance, withheld absolute top-10 revenue, and attributed margin dilution and PAT decline to one-time items and forex.
